children: Sporting goods retailer Dick’s Sporting Goods
will be reporting results this Tuesday before market open. Here’s what you need to know.

Dick's missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $5.59 billion, up 53.2% year on year. It was a sluggish quarter for the company, with full-year EPS guidance missing analysts’ expectations significantly and full-year revenue guidance slightly missing analysts’ expectations.
Is Dick's a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Dick’s revenue to grow 21.6% year on year, slowing from the 36.3% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Dick's has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Dick’s peers in the specialty retail segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Warby Parker delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 10.4%, meeting analysts’ expectations, and Bath and Body Works reported a revenue decline of 1.1%, topping estimates by 1%. Warby Parker traded up 19.7% following the results while Bath and Body Works was also up 1.1%.

params.linkText: Bath and Body Works’s results here

children: Investors in the specialty retail segment have had steady hands going into earnings, with share prices flat over the last month. Dick's is down 7.7% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $157.92 (compared to the current share price of $133.42).
